top_story: UN findings released on 26–27 October sharpened international legal pressure on Israel by framing its conduct in the West Bank as crimes against humanity and, more specifically, age-based persecution of Palestinian children, reinforcing a wider picture of systematic harm to civilians as the Gaza war continues. Those allegations land as Israelis vote on 27 October in an election that will determine whether Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition retains power, tying domestic political choice directly to the trajectory of occupation policy, military conduct, and Palestinian daily life. In parallel, British authorities charged two men over a plot targeting a UK airbase used by the United States and linked the case to Iran, underscoring how confrontation around Israel and Gaza continues to spill into wider regional and extra-regional security arenas. The combined picture is of a conflict system deepening on both the legal and political fronts, with civilians remaining the main constituency exposed to its consequences.
